en: The Apadāna of the Elder Umāpupphiya Chattavagga, Chapter Five, Number 5 [Verse 1] When the Buddha Kassapa was teaching the Dhamma, I was a young man named Jotipāla; I saw the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, Seated upon a seat beneath a tree. [Verse 2] Having seen him, I took a beautiful, fragrant *umā* flower, And offered it to the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One. Having made that offering, I spoke these words: "May I become like you, O Blessed One! [Verse 3] For eighty-four thousand aeons, I experienced the fruit of that merit. In the world of men, I was always honored, Possessing great wealth and abundant grain. [Verse 4] Now, in my final existence, I have been born in this human world. Having heard the Dhamma from the Conqueror, I have attained the state of an Arhat. [Verse 5] My bowl and robes are provided by others; I am one who has done what was to be done. Having seen the cessation of all formations, I dwell, having transcended birth and death. [Verse 6] This is the fruit of the *umā* flower, Offered long ago to the Great Sage. By this truth, may the world be well, And may the True Dhamma endure for a long time.
“When the Blessed One, the goal accomplished, the one honored by the world, the receiver of offerings, has entered Nibbāna;”
There was a festival for the Great Stupa.
While that festival was taking place,
[the relics] of the Great Seer Siddhattha [were enshrined].
I offered it upon the stupa.
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping a stupa.
there were eighty-five kings named Somadeva.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Umāpupphiya speak these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Umāpupphiya.
